text: A rule watching only CommonSecurityLog can't tell a routine vendor session from something worth attention. A rule watching only SigninLogs can't tell a travelling employee from something suspicious. Together, the two sources describe a narrower, more specific pattern.

This rule is named External RDP Allow Plus Entra Sign-In Correlation. It watches CommonSecurityLog for firewall allows reaching the internal RDP port, and SigninLogs for sign-ins, then flags any source address that appears in both, close together in time.
Two let statements build each half: RdpAllows filters CommonSecurityLog to allowed RDP connections in the last hour, and EntraSignIns filters SigninLogs over that same window.
A join kind equals inner on source IP against sign-in IP address lines the two sides up, and a where clause keeps only sign-ins landing after the firewall allow, within fifteen minutes.
This one rule is both the cross-source visibility Owen asked for and the documented, use-case-justified detection Renee needs. Next lesson configures a Conditional Access pilot policy.
